lesson.scenario: An API gateway allows bounded bursts using a bucket of ten tokens refilling at two tokens per second.
entities: Stores up to ten admission tokens
Adds two tokens per elapsed second

steps.title: Full bucket
steps.narration: After idle time, the bucket is capped at ten tokens.
steps.outcome: Ten immediate requests can be absorbed.
steps.invariant: Refill never raises the balance above capacity.

steps.title: Eight-request burst
steps.narration: Eight requests arrive together and reserve eight tokens atomically.
steps.outcome: The burst passes despite exceeding the steady two-per-second rate.
steps.invariant: Each admitted unit must decrement the shared balance exactly once.

steps.title: Four more arrive
steps.narration: Only two of four requests find tokens; two are rejected.
steps.outcome: Burst size is bounded by stored tokens.
steps.invariant: An empty bucket cannot admit work until refill creates balance.

steps.title: Time refills
steps.outcome: The limiter recovers according to elapsed time.
steps.invariant: Refill calculations should use monotonic elapsed time and be atomic with withdrawal.

steps.title: Steady traffic
steps.narration: Two requests consume two of the three available tokens.
steps.outcome: The bucket permits steady traffic while retaining one burst token.
steps.invariant: Distributed buckets require coordinated state or an explicitly approximate allocation scheme.

production.scenario: A courier-tracking platform in westus2 lets partner fleets burst reconnect-driven GPS updates into the dispatch pipeline while keeping each fleet on a steady ingest budget.
components: pushes batched GPS updates after drivers regain network coverage
owns partner telemetry intake for the dispatch platform
publishes burst and refill contracts for each fleet integration
admits short bursts while enforcing the steady ingest rate per fleet
authoritative sink for admitted driver location updates
stores shard leases and restart checkpoints for limiter partitions
stores excess bursts consumed by quota analytics and partner support workflows
flows: A partner fleet reconnects after tunnel loss and sends a burst of queued location updates.
fetch fleet rapid-courier quota plan rev 63
The API loads the current burst allowance and refill rate for the partner lane.
The control plane updates the limiter shard with the active fleet contract and rollout epoch.
request admission for batch GPS-4402 on fleet shard rc-3
The burst is evaluated by one limiter shard before any dispatch work is accepted.
Accepted location updates become durable dispatch telemetry events for route planning consumers.
Shard ownership and restart checkpoints are saved so a new pod can resume without losing limiter state.
emit throttle record for overflow from fleet rapid-courier
Overflow is preserved for replay and partner support instead of disappearing behind a 429 only.
